ranked_priorities.reason: Persistent Tmax >= 35 C, 44.0 C apparent heat, 25 warm nights, large exposed population, 25 hospitals, and only 12 shelters make immediate heat-health and night-recovery triage the strongest priority.
The Poyang/Yangtze low-water marker is about 100 days early, and elevated VPD plus 32 bridges and road context support water-level and access management.
VPD and persistent heat strongly justify drought monitoring, but this surveillance priority follows the direct heat-health and low-water response priorities.
Precipitation summaries alone do not explain the heat, VPD, warm-night, and early-low-water chain, and the package does not compute casualty, crop-loss, or economic-loss totals.

reasoning_path: Use the Open-Meteo daily and hourly file to compute persistent heat, apparent heat, warm nights, and VPD.
Use the NASA Poyang Lake report to recover the about 100-day early dry-season marker.
Use WorldPop and OSM files to add population, hospital, shelter, and bridge/access context.
Score all four candidate priorities with the normalized formula and rank by candidate priority score.
Reject rainfall-only or loss-accounting-first because it misses the heat-VPD-low-water mechanism and would overclaim losses not computed in the package.

criteria.description: Returns the requested JSON with target_family, package-relative source_files_used, computed values, score_formula, candidate priority scores, ranked priorities, top_priority cooling_health_and_night_recovery, and rejected_top_priority rainfall_only_or_loss_accounting_first.
criteria.name: ranking_schema_and_top_priority
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for a clear ranking object with minor schema drift or for the right top priority with incomplete secondary fields.

criteria.description: Computes the 17-day Tmax >= 35 C run, 44.0 C peak apparent heat, and 25 nights with Tmin >= 28 C, then uses them to support heat-health and night-recovery priority.
criteria.name: heat_health_calculation
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for two of the three values or for values within tolerance but weakly connected to the ranking.

criteria.description: Computes 84 July-August VPD hours above 2.5 kPa, recovers the about 100-day early Poyang/Yangtze low-water timing, and uses these to rank water management and drought monitoring.
criteria.name: hydrologic_and_vpd_calculation
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for one correct value plus a plausible hydrologic ranking argument.

criteria.description: Uses package exposure context: about 11,395,560 people, 25 hospitals, 12 shelters, and 32 bridges from local WorldPop/OSM files without turning them into confirmed casualties or outages.
criteria.name: exposure_and_access_context
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for using population plus either amenity or access context.

criteria.description: Produces the candidate scores 98.2, 95.0, 85.0, and 15.0, and ranks them in the correct order.
criteria.name: candidate_score_arithmetic_and_order
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for the correct order with small score drift, or for a correct top-two order with incomplete lower candidates.

criteria.description: Explains why rainfall-only or loss-accounting-first is not the top priority and avoids adding exact casualty, crop-loss, or economic-loss totals not computed from the package.
criteria.name: counterpriority_discipline
criteria.partial_credit: Give partial credit for rejecting the counterpriority but adding minor unsupported narrative.
